title: Can the China-US Detente Last?
gist: Trump and Xi's reciprocal visits produced talk of 'constructive strategic stability,' but the author argues agreement to manage rivalry is not agreement on terms, so the detente may be only a temporary adjustment in a longer strategic contest.

insights.claim: The Trump-Xi reciprocal visits and 'constructive strategic stability' language suggest both governments judge escalation too costly after years of tariffs, technology restrictions and mistrust.
insights.speaker: Yao Bowen
insights.so_what: Near-term de-escalation lowers tail risk for tariffs and export controls.

insights.claim: Because the underlying disputes behind confrontation remain unresolved, the detente could prove a temporary adjustment rather than a turning point in a longer strategic contest.
insights.speaker: Yao Bowen
insights.so_what: Do not price a permanent US-China thaw; keep hedges for renewed trade and tech tension.
insights.quote: agreement on the need to manage competition is not the same as agreement on its terms
